content: Your doctor has prescribed oxacillin, an antibiotic, to treat your infection. This medication will either be injected into a large muscle, such as your buttock or hip, or administered intravenously through a needle or catheter placed in your vein. The intravenous infusion typically lasts about 30 minutes and is given four to six times a day. Oxacillin works by eliminating bacteria responsible for infections, including pneumonia, meningitis, and infections of the urinary tract, skin, bones, joints, blood, and heart valves. In some cases, oxacillin may be prescribed for other uses; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Your healthcare provider may monitor the effectiveness of your treatment and check for side effects using laboratory tests and physical examinations. It is crucial to attend all scheduled appointments with your doctor and the laboratory. The duration of your treatment will depend on how your infection and symptoms respond to the medication. Precautions Before Taking Oxacillin: Inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to oxacillin, penicillin, cephalosporins, or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially antibiotics and vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have a history of asthma, hay fever, or kidney, liver, or gastrointestinal diseases (particularly colitis). Let your doctor know if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while taking oxacillin, contact your doctor immediately. If you have diabetes and regularly check your urine for sugar, use Clinistix or TesTape. Avoid using Clinitest tablets, as oxacillin may cause false-positive results. Administering Your Medication: Before using oxacillin, inspect the solution carefully. It should be clear and free of any floating particles. Gently squeeze the bag or examine the container to ensure there are no leaks. Do not use the solution if it is discolored, contains particles, or if the bag or container is leaking. Use a new solution and show the damaged one to your healthcare provider. It is essential to follow your healthcare provider's instructions precisely when using this medication. Do not stop your treatment prematurely, as this could worsen your infection and potentially lead to hospitalization. Do not alter your dosing schedule without consulting your healthcare provider. If you experience a mechanical problem, such as a blockage in the tubing, needle, or catheter, your healthcare provider may instruct you to stop the infusion. If this occurs, contact your healthcare provider immediately to ensure your therapy continues without interruption. Side Effects: Minor Side Effects: Oxacillin may cause mild side effects. Notify your healthcare provider if these symptoms are severe or persistent: Upset stomach Diarrhea Severe Side Effects: Contact your healthcare provider immediately if you experience any of the following symptoms: Rash Itching Fever Chills Facial swelling Wheezing Difficulty breathing Unusual bleeding or bruising Dizziness Seizures Sore mouth or throat If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor may report it to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Storing Your Medication: Your healthcare provider will likely supply you with several days' worth of oxacillin at a time. If you are receiving oxacillin intravenously, you will likely be instructed to store it in the refrigerator or freezer. Remove your next dose from the refrigerator one hour before use and place it in a clean, dry area to allow it to reach room temperature. If you are instructed to store additional oxacillin in the freezer, transfer a 24-hour supply to the refrigerator each day for the next day's use. Do not refreeze medications. If you are receiving oxacillin intramuscularly, your healthcare provider will provide specific storage instructions. Store your medication only as directed. Ensure you understand how to store it properly. Keep your supplies in a clean, dry place when not in use, and keep all medications and supplies out of reach of children. Your healthcare provider will instruct you on how to safely dispose of used needles, syringes, tubing, and containers to prevent accidental injury. In Case of Emergency or Overdose: If you suspect an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call 911 immediately. Signs of Infection: If you are receiving oxacillin intravenously or under your skin, it is important to recognize the symptoms of a catheter-related infection (an infection at the site where the needle enters your vein or skin).
